title: SciTrust: Evaluating the Trustworthiness of Large Language Models for Science
problem: Large language models exhibit hallucinations, inaccuracies, and biases when applied to scientific domains, necessitating comprehensive evaluation frameworks. There is a lack of domain-specific benchmarks and standardized metrics to assess LLM trustworthiness across scientific disciplines.
motivation: Deploying LLMs in scientific research requires rigorous evaluation of trustworthiness to ensure scientific integrity and reliable knowledge discovery.
method: SciTrust combines four domain-specific open-ended benchmarks spanning Computer Science, Chemistry, Biology, and Physics with a multi-faceted evaluation approach using both traditional metrics and LLM-based assessment. The framework evaluates five models including general-purpose and scientific-specific LLMs on tasks measuring truthfulness, accuracy, hallucination, and sycophancy, with performance and scalability evaluation on high-performance computing systems.
key_novelty: A comprehensive multi-disciplinary trustworthiness evaluation framework combining open-ended scientific benchmarks with hybrid LLM and traditional metrics to assess model reliability.
contributions: SciTrust evaluation framework for assessing LLM trustworthiness in scientific applications
Four novel open-ended scientific benchmarks covering Computer Science, Chemistry, Biology, and Physics
Comparative evaluation of five LLMs revealing nuanced strengths and weaknesses across models and domains
Open-sourced framework with datasets and scripts for reproducible research

metrics.accuracy: Model performance on truthfulness, accuracy, hallucination, and sycophancy benchmarks
metrics.other: Scalability and performance on HPC systems
